candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE for antineoplastic hazardous drugs
candidate.educational_objective: Use chemotherapy gloves and an appropriate protective gown when administering antineoplastic hazardous drugs, and add task-specific protective equipment when exposure risk warrants it.

options.A: Omit PPE when a closed-system drug-transfer device is used because engineering controls eliminate all exposure risk.
options.B: Use a surgical mask alone because room ventilation prevents skin exposure to liquid antineoplastic drugs.
options.C: Use ordinary examination gloves alone because chemotherapy gloves are needed only during drug compounding.
options.D: Wear chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent protective gown during administration, with additional eye, face, or respiratory protection when the task-specific exposure risk indicates it.

candidate.rationale: NIOSH states that during administration or compounding of antineoplastic drugs, healthcare workers should wear chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent gown with a closed front and tight-fitting cuffs. Engineering controls such as closed-system drug-transfer devices supplement exposure controls rather than eliminate PPE requirements. Additional protection is selected according to the route and likelihood of exposure. D is therefore the best answer; A through C provide inadequate protection.
candidate.source_claim_supported: During antineoplastic drug administration, NIOSH recommends chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent protective gown; engineering controls reduce but do not eliminate the need for appropriate exposure controls/PPE.
